verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a community report that Mastra's source is published under the Elastic License v2. That makes the source readable, but the license is source-available rather than OSI open, since it bars offering the software as a hosted or managed service. No first-party evidence in the pack makes an open-source claim to contradict, so 'disputed' is not supported; the restricted license is reflected as partial. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of the license and repository location, a license that is open without hosted-service restrictions, and independent hands-on confirmation that the source is publicly readable.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Mastra uses the Elastic v2 license, which says 'You may not provide the software to third parties as a hosted or managed service,'
